agree.reason: Marisol gets the late shelving report addressed head-on in the second paragraph, with monthly updates and a dated final report, plus a modest, believable target, so she would probably recommend yes; the main gap is that van running costs are never mentioned.

honest.reason: The draft correctly drops the unsupported 'double' claim and shows the true one-eighth figure, but it overstates a little: four drivers who 'said they would' become 'committed', 'cannot accept today' assumes the farms will offer again, and '610 households will go without it' goes beyond the facts.

works_the_facts.reason: Its figures all come from the brief and are shown in their best true form: 3,000 lb a month, 'risen by half' in the summer months, 10 to 15 lb per household, one-eighth across the year, three-quarters of the cost, and 'most' of the savings spent.

right_comparison.reason: The no-van alternative is shown accurately as refusing the same farm produce again, though 'all 610 households go without it' stretches the comparison and the target assumes farms will make the same offer.

qualification.reason: The first-year goal has a number (9,000 lb), a date (September 30, 2027) and a reporting promise for either outcome, but the only stated consequence of missing it is an explanation, and it doesn't say the goal depends on farms offering produce again.

objections.reason: It answers the obvious objections (the late report, the shrinking reserves, whether volunteers can keep the van running) without raising any that the brief already answers, but it leaves the fuel, insurance and maintenance question open.

fit.reason: This is a clearly sectioned grant narrative of about 475 words including headings, under the 500-word limit, though it leaves out the 'double' claim the director asked for, rightly, since the facts don't support it.
